contract_scope: The cumulative shipped 0.2.0 behavior boundary. The source is published under annotated tag v0.2.0; no GitHub Release, packaged distribution, or genuine clean-Mac run exists.

classifications.supported: Implemented in the current repository and backed by the listed local evidence.
classifications.interface_limited: Implemented only to the limit of supported macOS or vendor interfaces; the limitation is part of the contract.
classifications.deferred: Deliberately outside the implemented current behavior baseline or awaiting an external prerequisite.
classifications.excluded: Intentionally prohibited or out of scope for safety, privacy, cost, or product-policy reasons.

items.capability: Application catalog, inventory, capacity-aware planning, and Homebrew dry-run/apply routing
Machine-local runtime state with explicit override and verified legacy-state migration
Public, iCloud Private, machine-state, and secret configuration boundaries
iCloud/File Provider aware Git preflight and non-destructive materialization planning
Read-only application, permission, helper, service, extension, and background-task inventory
Allowlisted macOS preference capture, comparison, and explicitly confirmed application
Dock, startup-item, Chrome-profile, and device-specific K240 desired-state workflows
Portable DNS, SmartDNS opt-in, VPN, permission, and startup intent baseline
Plan-first app-specific cleanup inspection with explicit confirmation boundaries
Local bootstrap validation, fixture tests, compile checks, dry-run smoke, and Skill validation
Machine-validated transaction contracts for every supported mutation
Machine-enforced separation of reusable component guides from current-Mac observations
Tracked installation-source policy with pinned high-risk packages, executable-artifact checks, and machine-local provenance capture
Deterministic Clean-Mac acceptance harness with eligible-hardware attestation, gate ledger, sanitized evidence hashes, rollback requirement, and guarded finalization
Distinct repository-local macomrade CLI routing scan, plan, apply, verify, drift, diagnostics, and migration through compatibility-preserving scripts
Draft 2020-12 JSON contracts for catalog, settings, Private overlay, plan, state, and diagnostics with validation-before-use and non-destructive v0/v1 migrations
Allowlisted redacted diagnostic ZIP with versions, bounded logs, failure classes, public policy hashes, preview manifest, exact export confirmation, and ZIP read-back verification
Repeatable local cold/warm performance and resource benchmarks with absolute and regression budgets
Localized accessible terminal and static HTML audit views derived from existing read-only JSON evidence
Low-noise read-only drift monitoring with battery deferral, confidence filtering, severity cooldowns, and opt-in scheduling
TCC permission authorization and verification
items.limitation: macOS requires per-Mac visible authorization and does not expose a supported read/write API for every category.

items.capability: App Store, official-web, GUI installer, account, license, and first-launch completion
items.limitation: The skill may open and inspect supported surfaces, but secrets, purchases, security confirmations, and sign-in remain interactive.

items.capability: System Extension and Background Task Management inventory
items.limitation: The command may require administrator authorization or report an unavailable interface; unavailable is never interpreted as empty.

items.capability: Installation-source and provenance detection
items.limitation: Receipts, Homebrew metadata, bundle signatures, and paths provide evidence but cannot prove every historical installation source.

items.capability: VPN and network restoration
items.limitation: Client presence and desired DNS topology are portable; credentials, organization policy, network joins, and active connections are not.

items.capability: Display, audio, power, Night Shift, and True Tone capture/apply
items.limitation: Current macOS command interfaces do not provide a complete stable round-trip contract; observations remain read-only or deferred.

items.capability: Genuine unused/new-Mac release acceptance run
items.reason: Blocked on suitable hardware; three previously configured Macs are not clean-machine evidence.

items.capability: Deterministic schema-validated release-manifest preview binding source, public inputs, validation, benchmark, limitations, and non-authority

Memory-backed storage lifecycle with logical and allocated facts, iCloud metadata, decision expiry, target planning, transaction-bound cleanup, measured verification, Mole evidence, and non-authorizing OS/App handoffs
Browser/notes/SSH/photo lifecycle, productized application storage adapters, WeChat group lifecycle, iPhone organization, and native GUI
items.reason: Assigned to versions 0.3.0 through 1.0.0, not the implemented 0.2.0 baseline.

items.capability: Persisting passwords, tokens, private keys, recovery codes, cookies, sessions, raw TCC databases, or private payload content
items.reason: Protected secrets and private content never belong in Git or diagnostic configuration.

items.capability: Silent permission grants, account login, purchases, security confirmations, or destructive cleanup
items.reason: These operations require visible user authorization and verified read-back.

items.capability: Copying machine observations or TCC grants between Macs
items.reason: Only portable intent and iCloud Private preferences synchronize; every Mac creates and verifies its own runtime state.

items.capability: Hosted GitHub Actions as the default release quality gate
items.reason: The accepted policy uses local macOS validation; hosted runners do not represent the user's hardware, accounts, permissions, or GUI state.

items.capability: Relocating the repository out of iCloud as an implementation workaround
items.reason: iCloud/File Provider behavior is a supported operating constraint.

items.capability: Enabling SmartDNS or switching DNS to localhost by default
items.reason: Default DNS is 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8; SmartDNS requires an explicit user request.

items.capability: Automatic commit, push, tag, GitHub release, or App Store submission
items.reason: Every publication action requires separate explicit authorization.
